historicalBackground.origin: Historical evolution under the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and English common law.
historicalBackground.evolution: Transition from traditional common law rules of evidence to the statutory framework of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, and the modern codification under the Bharatiya Sakshya Sanhita (BSS), 2023.
historicalBackground.currentPosition: Governed by the Bharatiya Sakshya Sanhita, 2023 (BSS) which modernizes digital evidence and restructures section layouts.

concepts.name: General and Special Exceptions to burden of proof Secs. 108-116
concepts.meaning: Core concept of General and Special Exceptions to burden of proof Secs. 108-116 under Evidence Law.
concepts.purpose: To regulate the admissibility, relevancy, and reliability of evidence presented in court.
concepts.scope: Applies to judicial proceedings in court.
concepts.application: Used by judges to determine admissibility and weight of evidence.

concepts.name: Burden of Proof vs Onus of Proof
concepts.meaning: Burden of proof is the legal burden to establish a case (remains constant), whereas onus of proof is the evidentiary burden to introduce evidence (shifts).
concepts.purpose: To determine which party must lose if no evidence is given.

principles.name: Relevancy and Admissibility
principles.meaning: Evidence must be legally relevant to be admissible, but not all relevant evidence is admissible.
principles.importance: Ensures the court only considers reliable and legally obtained evidence.
principles.application: Used to filter out hearsay, character evidence, and privileged communications unless exceptions apply.

essentials.name: Legally Relevant
essentials.meaning: Must fall under the relevant sections of BSS (Sections 3 to 50).
essentials.proofRequirements: Logical connection to the facts in issue.
